The team's nickname. It rhymes with 'high', not 'hip'.

The club colours, worn since 1913.

lines.m: The Lanarkshire derby is the local game fans care about most.

lines.m: Fans' proudest boast about 2023-24.

lines.t: Köln is the one we have to win.
lines.m: The Rhine derby against Cologne is the big local game.

avoid.why: Bayer is German and rhymes with 'buyer'.
Bayern is Munich. Bayer is the company behind Leverkusen.

memory: 2022: Eintracht beat Rangers on penalties in Seville to win the Europa League

lingo.means: 'The Eagles', from the crest. A live golden eagle called Attila is the mascot.
Short for the club's old name, Sportgemeinde Eintracht. Fans use it everywhere.
'The Diva of the Main'. For a team that can beat anyone, or lose to anyone.
How locals refer to the club. English speakers usually just say Frankfurt.

lines.t: We took over the Camp Nou in 2022.
lines.m: Tens of thousands of Frankfurt fans went to Barcelona for a Europa League quarter-final.

lines.t: Seville 2022, best night of our lives.
lines.m: The Europa League final win over Rangers.

lines.t: Körbel played 602 Bundesliga games, all for us.
lines.m: No one has played more Bundesliga matches.

lines.t: Forget Bayern, Offenbach is the one.
lines.m: The local rivalry with Kickers Offenbach matters most to old-school fans.

avoid.why: Fans call the club Eintracht, never 'Frankfurt FC'.
The 'ch' is a throaty sound, like in 'loch'.

memory: 2025: PSG won their first Champions League, beating Inter 5-0 in the final in Munich

lingo.means: 'This is Paris', the club slogan and the fans' favourite cry.
Short for the Parc des Princes, home since 1974.
'The Parisians', a common nickname for the team.
How French fans say it. English speakers say P-S-G.

lines.t: Ici c'est Paris!
lines.m: The club slogan and the go-to chant.

lines.t: Le Classique is the game that matters.
lines.m: Games against Marseille are the biggest in France.

lines.t: Nothing in France sounds like the Parc.
lines.m: Fans rate their home atmosphere the best in the country.

lines.t: Munich 2025, we finally did it.
lines.m: The first Champions League title after years of near misses.

avoid.why: It's French: the G is soft and the final N is nasal.
Paris FC are the city's other top-flight club, a separate team.

memory: 1993: Marseille beat AC Milan 1-0 in Munich and became the first French club to win the Champions League

lingo.means: Short for Olympique de Marseille. How everyone in France refers to the club.
'Straight for goal', the club motto on the crest.
'Forever the first'. Fans' reminder that they won the Champions League before any other French club.
Nickname from the ancient Greeks of Phocaea, who founded Marseille.

lines.t: Allez l'OM!
lines.m: 'Come on OM!' The basic cheer.

lines.t: À jamais les premiers.
lines.m: Forever the first: 1993 still beats anything Paris have done.

lines.t: The Vélodrome is the loudest ground in France.
lines.m: Fans take huge pride in their home atmosphere.

lines.t: Paris has the money, we have the passion.
lines.m: Mild banter aimed at PSG.

avoid.why: Nobody uses the full name in conversation.
The '-eille' ending is said like 'ay'.

memory: 2002-2008: Lyon won seven French titles in a row, still a record

lingo.means: Lyon dialect for 'the kids'. The team's nickname; the biggest fan group is the Bad Gones.
Short for Olympique Lyonnais. English speakers just say Lyon.
Locals call the Saint-Étienne game simply 'the Derby'.

lines.t: Allez l'OL!
lines.m: 'Come on Lyon!' The basic cheer.

lines.t: Seven titles in a row. Nobody else in France has done that.
lines.m: The 2002 to 2008 run is a French record.

lines.t: Juninho's free kicks were works of art.
lines.m: Juninho scored a club-record 44 free kicks.

lines.t: Beat Saint-Étienne and nothing else matters.
lines.m: The Derby du Rhône is the game Lyon fans care about most.

avoid.why: In French, Lyon has two syllables and a soft, nasal N.
The full name is Olympique Lyonnais, and fans just say l'OL.

memory: 2004: Monaco knocked out Real Madrid and Chelsea on the way to the Champions League final

lingo.means: Monegasque for 'Come on Monaco'. Printed on shirts and posted after every game.
'The Monegasques', the team's nickname.
'The Rock', a nickname from Monaco's rocky headland.
Short for the Stade Louis II, the stadium with the famous arches.

lines.t: Daghe Munegu!
lines.m: Fans' cheer in the local Monegasque language.

lines.t: Small stadium, big European nights.
lines.m: The ground is small but has hosted famous wins.

lines.t: Our academy gives the world its stars.
lines.m: Fans are proud of the young players Monaco develop and sell.

lines.t: Beating Nice down the coast is what counts.
lines.m: Mild banter about the nearby rival.

avoid.instead: Monaco play in the French league
avoid.why: Monaco is its own country. The club just plays in Ligue 1.
In French the numeral is said 'deux'.

unsure: rivals: Nice is the nearby rival, but I couldn't confirm a fixed name for the derby, so derby is left blank
